ai-at-work.excerpt: This latest lawsuit is particularly broad and homes in on accusations of illegal piracy.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Sony Music and Warner Bros are suing Anthropic for allegedly scraping massive amounts of copyrighted music data to train Claude without permission. This matters because every organization using generative AI now has to reckon with the legal liability of what their tools were trained on, and you could be caught in the crosshairs of IP disputes you didn't create. Here's the thing though: these lawsuits are basically the music industry finally realizing that "move fast and break things" was never supposed to apply to their catalogs.

ai-at-work.dwp_take: Owner.com, a restaurant management software company, just closed a $240 million Series D funding round led by Goldman Sachs. digital-culture.dwp_take: A new survey of 1,250 U.S. workers found that AI isn't delivering the mass job apocalypse everyone predicted, with some roles actually seeing productivity gains and new opportunities. digital-culture.title: AI Has Human Doctors Asking: What’s Left for Us?
digital-culture.excerpt: A recent paper argues that AI is often better at doctoring than doctors. Guess who isn't thrilled.
digital-culture.dwp_take: A new research paper suggests AI diagnostic systems are outperforming human doctors in several medical tasks, which has understandably spooked the medical profession. This matters to digital workplace folks because it's the same anxiety playing out across every knowledge worker industry right now, from legal to accounting to your friendly neighborhood business analyst. Here's the thing though: I've seen this movie before, and the ending isn't "robots replace everyone" but rather "people who learn to work with the tools win."

digital-culture.title: Tech Visionary Says the Big AI Labs Don’t Get What People Want
digital-culture.excerpt: Tim O’Reilly built a publishing empire that AI is helping to destroy. Yet he loves AI—as long as it’s open source.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Tim O'Reilly is arguing that closed proprietary AI from the big labs misses what users actually need, and that open source AI is the better path forward. This matters to digital workplace pros because the tools shaping how we work, communicate, and solve problems are increasingly AI-powered, and whether those tools are locked down or open has real implications for enterprise flexibility and innovation. Here's the thing though: O'Reilly's got skin in the game with open source, so take his "the incumbents don't get it" speech with a grain of salt, even if he's not entirely wrong.

industry-news.excerpt: See what you missed in Daily Tech Insider from August 24–28. The post AI Expansion Meets Security Crises, Costs, and Public Resistance in Tech This Week appeared first on TechRepublic.
industry-news.dwp_take: Companies are rolling out AI tools at breakneck speed while simultaneously dealing with security breaches, ballooning costs, and pushback from employees and the public. For those of us building digital workplaces, this means we're being asked to integrate AI solutions that haven't been properly secured or budgeted for, all while our users are already exhausted by tech change. The irony is thick: we're promising productivity gains from AI while creating new security headaches and worker skepticism that might actually kill adoption.
